From Proto-Albanian *bardza (“white”). Cognate to Aromanian bardzu (“white (of horses and mules)”).
Possibly from a hypothetical Proto-Albanian *mandjā, which would have been the female equivalent of the word which gave mânz.

From older vied̦ure, possibly from Late Proto-Albanian *vedzula, a deverbative of Proto-Albanian *wedza (“to steal”). The declension signals that the etymon is likely to have contained the Proto-Albanian diminutive suffix *-ula with the final vowel preserved. Romanian mazăre (“peas”) certainly resul
